mainTopic: The tannery away from the west side of the city, the debate over where the שכינה rests, and the four winds
overview: This amud opens with the last words of the previous discussion: chaff harms a field because it acts like too much manure. A new משנה then rules that carcasses, graves, and a בורסקי (tannery) must be kept fifty אמות from a city. The תנא קמא allows a tannery only on the east side, and רבי עקיבא allows any side except the west. The משנה also lists things that must be kept away from what they damage. The גמרא asks how to read רבי עקיבא, and a ברייתא shows that the west is banned completely because it is 'frequent'. רבא asks what 'frequent' means. The גמרא rejects the idea that the west wind blows most and explains it as 'frequent with the שכינה'. It then brings a debate over whether the שכינה is in every place or in the west. Finally, רב יהודה reads a פסוק as describing the four winds, and a ברייתא of רבי אליעזר about the world begins and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The chaff turns the field into manure
steps.stepSummary: The last words of the previous discussion give the reason for the damage: the chaff acts like manure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it turns it into manure.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes the previous discussion. It explains that chaff blowing onto a neighbor's land damages it because it acts like manure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Manure is normally good for a field, but too much of it damages seeds. The point is that the chaff causes real harm, which is why it must be kept away.

keyTerms.meaning: Turns it into, makes it into

phrases.english: For it turns it into manure.
phrases.notes: This closes a discussion from the previous page. The chaff acts like manure, and too much manure ruins seeds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the discussion from the previous page.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The damage comes from the chaff acting like an excess of manure.

steps.title: Carcasses, graves, and tanneries must be kept 50 אמות from the city
steps.stepSummary: The משנה requires a distance of fifty אמות for carcasses, graves, and a בורסקי. The תנא קמא allows a tannery only on the east side, while רבי עקיבא allows any side except the west.
steps.simpleTranslation: One must keep animal carcasses, graves, and a tannery fifty אמות away from the city. A tannery may only be set up on the east side of the city. רבי עקיבא says: one may set it up on any side except the west, and he must keep it fifty אמות away.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It rules that bad-smelling or unpleasant things must be kept fifty אמות away from a city, and it presents a disagreement about which side of the city a tannery may be built on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The winds usually blow from the west, so a tannery on the east side sends its smell away from the city. The תנא קמא allows only the east side. רבי עקיבא is more lenient and allows any side except the west, since a west wind would blow the smell straight into the city.

keyTerms.meaning: A tannery, where animal hides are processed (very smelly)
A cubit, a measure of roughly half a meter

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume רבי עקיבא is simply repeating the תנא קמא. The תנא קמא allows only the east, while רבי עקיבא allows north, south, and east, ruling out only the west.

phrases.english: MISHNAH
One must distance animal carcasses
and graves, and a tannery
from the city, fifty cubits.
One may not make a tannery
except on the east side of the city.
Rabbi Akiva says:
On any side he may make it,
except for its west side;
and he distances it fifty cubits.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַרְחִיקִין אֶת הַנְּבֵלוֹת וְאֶת הַקְּבָרוֹת וְאֶת הַבּוּרְסְקִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic, keeping nuisances away from the city.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Carcasses, graves, and a tannery must be fifty אמות from the city. The תנא קמא allows a tannery only on the east side. רבי עקיבא allows any side except the west, with a fifty-אמה distance.

steps.title: Keeping harmful crops and items away from a neighbor's produce
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds more pairs that must be kept apart: flax-soaking water from vegetables, leeks from onions, and mustard from bees. רבי יוסי permits the mustard.
steps.simpleTranslation: One must keep flax-soaking water away from vegetables, leeks away from onions, and mustard away from bees. רבי יוסי permits it in the case of mustard.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with cases where one thing damages a neighbor's crop or animals, so it must be kept away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each pair names a damager and the thing it damages: the soaking water ruins vegetables, leeks harm onions, and mustard harms bees. רבי יוסי disagrees only about mustard and does not require distancing it.

keyTerms.meaning: Water used to soak flax, which harms plants

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's rule is to keep the damaging thing away from what it harms. רבי יוסי disagrees only about mustard and bees.

phrases.english: And one must distance flax-soaking water from vegetables,
and leeks from onions,
and mustard from bees.
And Rabbi Yosei permits in the case of mustard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה with more cases of required distancing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Damaging items must be kept away from what they harm. רבי יוסי permits mustard near bees.

steps.title: What exactly did רבי עקיבא mean about the west side?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי עקיבא means the west side only needs fifty אמות of distance, or that the west side is not allowed at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: how does רבי עקיבא mean it? Does he mean one may build a tannery on any side, even right next to the city, except the west, where he must keep it fifty אמות away? Or does he mean one may build on any side as long as he keeps it fifty אמות away, except the west, where he may not build it at all?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises an איבעיא about how to read רבי עקיבא's words in the משנה. It offers two possible readings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'except the west' and 'distance fifty אמות' can be connected in two ways. In the first reading, other sides need no distance and the west needs fifty אמות. In the second reading, every allowed side needs fifty אמות and the west is banned completely.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them (the Sages)
Places it close, right next to the city

steps.confusionAlert: Both readings agree that the west is the worst side. They argue only about whether the west needs distance or is banned entirely, and whether the other sides need distance at all.

phrases.english: GEMARA
A question was raised before them:
Rabbi Akiva, how does he mean it?
On any side he may make it and place it close,
except for its west side,
where he distances fifty cubits and then makes it;
or perhaps:
On any side he may make it
and distance it fifty cubits,
except for its west side,
where he may not make it at all?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא הֵיכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רבי עקיבא's words in the משנה to clarify their meaning.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי עקיבא's fifty-אמה rule applies to the west side only, with other sides allowed close, or to all permitted sides, with the west banned entirely.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows the west side is banned completely
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי עקיבא clearly: build on any side with fifty אמות of distance, but never on the west, because it is 'frequent'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear, as it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי עקיבא says, one may build it on any side and keep it fifty אמות away, except the west side, where he may not build it at all, because it is frequent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a ברייתא that states רבי עקיבא's opinion clearly. It proves the second reading is correct.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's wording 'not at all' settles the question. Every allowed side needs fifty אמות, and the west is completely forbidden. It also gives a one-word reason, that the west is 'frequent' (תדירא), and steps 6–8 work out what that word means.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear, introducing a proof
As it was taught in a ברייתא

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי עקיבא, a tannery may be built on any side of the city except the west, always fifty אמות away. The west is banned completely because it is 'frequent'. The גמרא explains this word in the next steps.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
As it was taught: Rabbi Akiva says:
On any side he may make it
and distance it fifty cubits,
except for its west side,
where he may not make it at all,
because it is frequent.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: The second reading of רבי עקיבא: fifty אמות on all allowed sides, and the west banned entirely.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting רבי עקיבא with the words 'not at all' and the reason that the west is 'frequent'.

steps.title: רבא asks what 'frequent' means
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks רב נחמן what the word תדירא in the ברייתא means.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to רב נחמן: What does 'frequent' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא asks what רבי עקיבא meant when he called the west 'frequent'. This question sets up the next moves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 gave the reason for not building on the west: it is 'frequent'. That word is unclear. 'Frequent' in what way? רבא wants it defined.

phrases.english: Rava said to Rav Nachman:
What does 'frequent' mean?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא לְרַב נַחְמָן: מַאי תְּדִירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the reason given in the ברייתא of step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In what sense is the west 'frequent'?

steps.title: It cannot mean the west wind blows the most
steps.stepSummary: If 'frequent' meant the west wind blows most often, that conflicts with רב, who taught that the northern wind blows together with every other wind.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means frequent among the winds, didn't רב חנן בר אבא say in רב's name: Four winds blow every day, and the northern wind blows with all of them, because without it the world could not last even one hour. And the southern wind is the harshest, and if not for בן נץ holding it back, it would destroy the world, as it says: 'Is it by your understanding that the hawk soars, spreading its wings toward the south?'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא, asking רב נחמן, tries the obvious reading, that the west wind blows the most. It rejects that reading using a teaching of רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב taught that all four winds blow every day, and the northern wind joins every one of them. So the northern wind is the most constant, not the western wind. That means 'frequent' must mean something else.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say, suppose it means
But didn't (so-and-so) say? A challenge from another teaching
Ben Netz, an angel who holds back the southern wind

phrases.english: If you say it means frequent among the winds,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אָמַר רַב חָנָן בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: but didn't Rav Chanan bar Abba say in the name of Rav:
Four winds blow every day,
and the northern wind blows with all of them;
for if it were not so,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין הָעוֹלָם מִתְקַיֵּים אֲפִילּוּ שָׁעָה אַחַת.
phrases.english: the world would not survive even one hour.
And the southern wind is the harshest of them all,
and if not for Ben Netz, who holds it back,
it would destroy the world,
as it says: 'Is it by your understanding that the hawk soars,'
'spreading its wings toward the south?'
phrases.notes: איוב 39:26. Here תימן means 'south', and נץ (hawk) is read as the angel's name.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא תְּדִירָא בְּרוּחוֹת, וְהָא אָמַר רַב חָנָן בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers the first possible answer to step 6 and knocks it down.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading 'frequent' as the west wind blowing most often
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב taught that the northern wind joins all the other winds, so it is the most constant wind, not the western one.

steps.title: Frequent means the שכינה is in the west
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the west is 'frequent with the שכינה'. It proves this from רבי יהושע בן לוי, who reads the פסוק about the heavenly hosts bowing as showing that we pray toward the west.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what does 'frequent' mean? Frequent with the Divine Presence. As רבי יהושע בן לוי said: Come, let us thank our ancestors, who taught us the place of prayer, as it is written: 'And the host of heaven bow to You.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new meaning: the שכינה is found in the west. So a smelly tannery should not face that direction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע בן לוי says the sun, moon and stars bow to ה׳. Since they move from east to west, they bow toward the west. That shows the שכינה is in the west, and this explains why רבי עקיבא forbids a בורסקי there.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather: introduces a new explanation after rejecting the old one
The direction to face in prayer
The host of heaven: sun, moon and stars

phrases.english: Rather, what does 'frequent' mean?
Frequent with the Divine Presence.
As Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
Come, let us thank our ancestors,
who taught us the place of prayer,
as it is written: 'And the host of heaven bow to You.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the reading that step 7 rejected with a new one.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Frequent' means the שכינה is in the west, so a foul-smelling tannery should not be placed there.
steps.whyThisMatters: This links a damages law about tanneries to a principle about honoring the place of the שכינה.

steps.title: Maybe the stars bow while walking backward
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב challenges the proof: the heavenly hosts might be bowing toward the east while moving backward to the west, like a servant leaving his master. The גמרא leaves this as a קשיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב challenged it: But maybe they are like a servant who receives a gift from his master and walks backward while bowing! It is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב attacks the proof from the פסוק. The גמרא admits it has no answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A servant leaving his master walks backward so that he keeps facing him. In the same way, the stars may face east, toward the שכינה, while they move west. Then the פסוק proves nothing about the west, and the word קשיא tells us the challenge stands.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult: the challenge stays unanswered

steps.confusionAlert: קשיא here does not mean the law about the west is cancelled. It means only that this proof from the פסוק is weakened.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב:
phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Yaakov challenged it:
But maybe they are like a servant who receives a gift from his master,
and walks backward while bowing!
phrases.notes: He means the stars could be facing east while moving west, so the שכינה could be in the east.

phrases.english: It is difficult.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proof from the פסוק in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע בן לוי's proof that the שכינה is in the west
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The stars' westward movement could be backward walking while they face east, so the פסוק does not prove the west.

steps.title: רבי אושעיא: the שכינה is in every place
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings רבי אושעיא's view that the שכינה is everywhere. He learns it from the פסוק about lightning: lightning goes out and reports from wherever it was sent.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אושעיא holds the שכינה is in every place. As רבי אושעיא said: What is meant by 'You alone are ה׳, You made the heavens, etc.'? Your messengers are not like human messengers. Human messengers return to report to the place they were sent from. But Your messengers report from the very place they were sent to, as it says: 'Can you send out lightning bolts, so they go and say to you: Here we are?' It does not say 'they will come and say' but 'they go and say,' teaching that the שכינה is in every place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a different opinion. רבי אושעיא holds the שכינה is not in one direction but everywhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A human messenger must travel back to his sender in order to report. The פסוק says lightning 'goes and says,' meaning it reports from where it already is. So ה׳ is there too, and the שכינה is in every place, which goes against the idea that it is only in the west.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two views. The view behind רבי עקיבא's ruling holds that the שכינה is especially in the west, which is why there is no tannery on the west side. רבי אושעיא holds the שכינה is in every place.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Oshaya holds:
The Divine Presence is in every place.
As Rabbi Oshaya said,
What is meant by what is written: 'You alone are ה׳,'
'You made the heavens, etc.'?
phrases.notes: נחמיה 9:6, the same פסוק used in step 8.

phrases.english: Your messengers are not like messengers of flesh and blood;
messengers of flesh and blood,
from the place they are sent from,
to there they return to report on their mission;
but Your messengers,
the place they are sent to,
from there they report on their mission,
as it says: 'Can you send out lightning bolts'
'so they go and say to you: Here we are?'
It does not say 'they will come and say,'
but rather 'they go and say,'
which teaches that the Divine Presence is in every place.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא סָבַר: שְׁכִינָה בְּכׇל מָקוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents an opposing view to step 8's claim that the שכינה is in the west.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אושעיא holds the שכינה is in every place, learned from lightning that 'goes and says' rather than 'comes and says'.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל also holds the שכינה is everywhere
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that the school of רבי ישמעאל agrees with רבי אושעיא. The proof comes from a פסוק in זכריה, where a second angel goes out "to meet" the first angel.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל also holds that the שכינה is in every place. His school taught: How do we know the שכינה is everywhere? The פסוק says, "Behold, the angel who spoke with me went out, and another angel went out to meet him." It does not say "after him" but "to meet him." This teaches that the שכינה is everywhere.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second supporter for רבי אושעיא's view that the שכינה is everywhere. It brings a teaching from the school of רבי ישמעאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both angels came from one fixed place, the second one would follow "after" the first. The פסוק says the second angel came "to meet him," which means from the opposite side. So angels set out from different directions, which shows the שכינה is in every place.

keyTerms.meaning: And also. This signals that another person agrees with the view just mentioned.
A teaching from the study hall (school) of רבי ישמעאל
From where do we know? This asks for a source.
To meet him, coming toward him from the other side

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yishmael, too, holds
that the Divine Presence is in every place.
As the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
From where do we know that the Divine Presence is in every place?
As it is stated: "And behold, the angel who spoke with me went out,
and another angel went out to meet him."
It does not say "after him,"
but rather "to meet him,"
which teaches that the Divine Presence is in every place.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל סָבַר שְׁכִינָה בְּכׇל מָקוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another תנא who agrees with רבי אושעיא's view from Step 10.
steps.raayaObject: The view that the שכינה is in every place
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא from the school of רבי ישמעאל, reading לקראתו in זכריה 2:7

steps.title: רב ששת also holds the שכינה is everywhere
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת told his servant to face him in any direction for prayer except east. He explained that this was not because the שכינה is missing from the east, but because heretics teach people to pray toward the east.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת also holds that the שכינה is in every place. He told his servant: "Stand me facing any direction except east. This is not because the שכינה is not there, but because the heretics teach people to face that way."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third supporter, רב ששת, and shows from how he prayed that he held the שכינה is everywhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת was willing to pray facing any direction, so he did not think the שכינה sits in one special direction. He avoided the east only so that he would not look like the מינים. He made clear that this was not because the east lacks the שכינה.

keyTerms.meaning: Stand me up, set me in place

steps.confusionAlert: רב ששת's avoiding the east does not mean he thought the שכינה was missing there. The text says so outright. He only wanted to stay away from the practice of the מינים.

phrases.english: And Rav Sheshet, too, holds
that the Divine Presence is in every place.
As Rav Sheshet said to his servant:
Set me facing any direction,
except for the east.
And this is not because the Divine Presence is not there,
but because the heretics instruct people to pray in that direction.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף רַב שֵׁשֶׁת סָבַר שְׁכִינָה בְּכׇל מָקוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an אמורא who agrees, after the תנא in Step 11.
steps.raayaObject: The view that the שכינה is in every place
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב ששת's instruction to his servant about which direction to face in prayer

steps.title: רבי אבהו: the שכינה is in the west
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו disagrees and says the שכינה is in the west. He reads the word אוריה, a name for the west, as אויר יה, "the air of God."
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי אבהו says the שכינה is in the west. He explains: what does the word "אוריה" mean? It means "אויר יה," the air of God.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now brings the opposite view: רבי אבהו holds that the שכינה has a special place, the west.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 10 to 12 said the שכינה is everywhere. רבי אבהו goes back to the idea from Step 8 that the west is connected to the שכינה. He supports it by splitting the word אוריה into two words: אויר (air) and יה (God's name).
steps.whatToRemember: There are two views. רבי אושעיא, רבי ישמעאל, and רב ששת hold that the שכינה is in every place. רבי אבהו holds that the שכינה is in the west.

phrases.english: But Rabbi Abbahu says:
The Divine Presence is in the west.
As Rabbi Abbahu said:
What is the meaning of "oriyah"?
phrases.notes: אוריה is a word used for the west.

phrases.english: The air of God.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents the view opposing Steps 10–12 and brings back the idea from Step 8 that the שכינה is in the west.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שכינה is in the west, because the west is called אוריה, meaning אויר יה.

steps.title: רב יהודה: the western wind comes from the back of the world
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה explains the פסוק "יערף כמטר לקחי" as referring to the western wind. The word יערף hints at עורף, the back of the neck, because the west is the back of the world.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: What does the פסוק "My teaching shall drop like the rain" mean? This refers to the western wind, which comes from the back of the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a related teaching about the four winds. רב יהודה connects a פסוק to the western wind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word יערף sounds like עורף, meaning the back of the neck. רב יהודה reads the פסוק as talking about the wind from the west, which he calls the back of the world. This adds another idea about the west to the discussion of winds.

keyTerms.meaning: What is meant by what is written? This opens an explanation of a פסוק.
Shall drop. It sounds like עורף.
The back of the neck, the back side

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
What is the meaning of that which is written:
"My teaching shall drop like the rain"?
This is the western wind,
which comes from the back of the world.
phrases.notes: This is a play on words: יערף sounds like עורף, "the back."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from where the שכינה is to a teaching about the western wind, staying with the theme of the four winds.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: "יערף כמטר לקחי" refers to the western wind, which comes from the עורף (back) of the world.

steps.title: The second phrase of the verse refers to the northern wind
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה continues explaining the פסוק. He reads "תזל כטל אמרתי" as the northern wind, which "makes gold cheap" (מזלת). He supports the meaning of the word from a פסוק in ישעיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: "My speech shall distill like the dew": this is the northern wind, which makes gold cheap. And so it says: "Those who pour out gold from the bag."
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה moves to the next phrase of the same פסוק and connects it to the northern wind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word תזל sounds like מזלת, which means "makes cheap." The dry north wind lowers the crops, so food becomes expensive and gold is worth less. The פסוק in ישעיה shows that the root זל can mean treating gold as cheap.

keyTerms.meaning: Will drip or flow down. The verse uses it about speech falling like dew.
Makes cheap, lowers the value of
Those who pour out or spend freely, treating gold as cheap

phrases.english: "My speech shall distill like the dew"
phrases.notes: דברים 32:2, the same פסוק as step 14.

phrases.english: this is the northern wind,
which makes gold cheap.
And so it says:
"Those who pour out gold from the bag."

steps.triggerLanguage: תזל כטל אמרתי זו רוח צפונית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב יהודה's line-by-line reading of the same פסוק, moving from the west wind to the north wind.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: "תזל כטל" refers to the northern wind, which lowers the value of gold.

steps.title: The last two phrases refer to the eastern and southern winds
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה finishes the פסוק. "כשעירם עלי דשא" is the eastern wind, which storms through the world like a שעיר. "וכרביבים עלי עשב" is the southern wind, which brings rain showers and makes plants grow.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Like light rains on the grass": this is the eastern wind, which storms through the whole world like a demon. "And like showers on the herbs": this is the southern wind, which brings up showers and makes herbs grow.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה finishes matching the phrases of the פסוק to the four winds by covering east and south.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שעירם sounds like שעיר (a demon) and מסערת (storms). That fits the strong, harsh eastern wind. רביבים are rain showers, and the southern wind brings them up and makes עשב grow, just as the פסוק says.

keyTerms.meaning: Light rains. Here it is read as a play on שָׂעִיר and "storming."

steps.whatToRemember: The whole פסוק "יערף כמטר לקחי" is read as the four winds: west (יערף), north (תזל), east (שעירם), and south (רביבים).

phrases.english: "Like light rains on the grass"
this is the eastern wind,
which storms through the whole world
like a demon.
phrases.notes: A play on words: שעירם, מסערת and שעיר all sound alike.

phrases.english: "And like showers on the herbs"
this is the southern wind,
which brings up showers
and makes herbs grow.

steps.triggerLanguage: כשעירם עלי דשא זו רוח מזרחית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the reading of the פסוק that began in steps 14 and 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: "כשעירם" is the stormy eastern wind, and "כרביבים" is the southern wind that brings rain and growth.

steps.title: Opening of רבי אליעזר's teaching about the world
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא in which רבי אליעזר begins to describe the world. Only the opening words appear here, and the statement continues in the next part.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי אליעזר says: The world...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move by starting a new ברייתא from רבי אליעזר. His full statement comes in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the four winds, the גמרא turns to a new teaching of רבי אליעזר that begins with the word 'world'. Only the opening word appears on this amud, and his full statement comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
A תנא whose teaching is quoted here

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Eliezer says:
The world
phrases.notes: The sentence keeps going on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the four winds to a new ברייתא about the shape of the world.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר begins a statement about the world. It is completed in the next part of the text.
